# CI dependency proxy

CI jobs start a local HTTP repository for Gradle, OCI, npm, PyPI and approved binary downloads. `proxy.cjs` defines the supported upstreams and maps repository paths to them. A public pull request reads an index and fetches verified objects from GitHub Actions Cache as its tools request them. It uses no AWS credentials. The isolated Linux protocol check runs in a separate network namespace and exposes a single read-only artifact broker socket. Existing native Docker jobs use their disposable runner daemon and have the normal hosted runner network permissions.

## Runtime bootstrap

Enabled Gradle, kind migration, and Compose jobs request the Corretto 21.0.13.1.2 JDK archive for their operating system and architecture through `/raw/corretto/`. Each worker verifies the SHA-256 from the Corretto release before giving the archive to `actions/setup-java` as a local JDK. The Linux protocol seed runs that JDK and Gradle. The macOS build records its own archive when it runs on protected main. Python-only and npm-only test jobs skip JDK provisioning when the proxy is enabled. Update the version and the four archive digests together in `corretto.cjs`.

The migration kind installer fetches its pinned binary through `/raw/kind/`. The Python console integration uses `helm/kind-action` to bootstrap its cluster and uses `/raw/argo/` for the Argo manifest. The K3s integration uses a `rancher/k3s` image through the Docker registry route. `/raw/k3s/` serves explicit K3s release file requests. The GitHub runner, GitHub Actions themselves, Node/npm, the cache toolkit, and the Python interpreter use their normal bootstrap paths. Once the broker starts, npm package files, pip and Pipenv packages, the Gradle distribution, and supported image manifests and layers use the job-local proxy.

## Protected main publication

Each enabled main worker records the public paths, timestamps, and digests that its dependency clients actually accessed, including known missing optional metadata. The native worker writes its receipt alongside its results. Hosted workers hand off a bounded receipt through their main-scoped Actions cache. The main observer dispatches a serialized publisher as worker receipts arrive. The Oregon publisher validates receipts, verifies bytes from fixed public origins, and updates a private S3 catalog. It selects up to **30,000,000,000 unique bytes** by most recent main access. Aliased content counts once. It groups small files, reuses unchanged GitHub entries, and publishes the immutable index last. A cache miss in a PR names the missing path and fails locally. A new version published only in a PR must be warmed by a trusted job before it is available in the shared working set. GitHub may evict old entries independently. Re-dispatch the publisher to repair evicted entries from the durable store.

`Publish main dependency cache` accepts `seed=true` to exercise native clients and bootstrap an empty store. A `Dependency cache protocol check` dispatch with `record=true` tests the main-worker handoff. Dispatch without `record` to test lazy playback. Enable the repository variable `DEPENDENCY_PROXY_ENABLED=true` after bootstrapping. An upstream fork without the Oregon infrastructure can leave the variable unset. The same local protocol can be exercised without AWS using `CI_DEPENDENCY_RECEIPT=/tmp/receipt.json node .github/ci/dependency-cache/cli.cjs record-worker -- <command>`. Common endpoints include `/maven/`, `/npm/`, `/pypi/simple/`, `/raw/kubectl/`, and `/v2/dockerhub/`. A native OCI image can be pulled as `127.0.0.1:<port>/dockerhub/library/hello-world`.

The protected launcher uses GitHub OIDC to start the `migrations-main-dependency-cache` CodeBuild project in `us-west-2`. It passes a short-lived GitHub cache grant through a unique SSM SecureString. The worker deletes it immediately after retrieval and only executes a commit verified reachable from protected `main`. The launcher never reads the S3 store and PR workers cannot write the durable catalog. GitHub cache contents are readable from public fork PRs. Store only public dependencies and origin-relative paths. Never add an authenticated package feed or private download to the public catalog.
